##### Homogeneous network interference

We introduce the assumption of [*homogeneous network interference*](#def-homogenous-network-interference), which reduces the complexity of network exposure mappings. This assumption holds that for any node in the network, the effect of a neighbor’s treatment is the same regardless of which neighbor it is, and regardless of the position of the unit in the network.  In addition, network exposure mappings are restricted so that their values lie in a finite set. A structural equation shows homogenous network  interference obtains if it is [separable](#def-separatability) with [positionally invariant](#def-positional-invariance) and [bounded](#def-boundedness) coponent functions.
